JUDGMENT

By this judgment this Tribunal shall decide the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 04.01.2023 at about 3.30 pm., petitioner was walking on the extreme left side on Sarjapura main road near Lakasa Restaurant, Jayaram Reddy Layout,
Kasavanahalli, Bengaluru, at that time driver of one Car bearing reg.No.KL-22-H-9642 came from behind in reverse gear in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused accident.
3.

Due to this, petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, he has sustained right ankle, medial malleolus fracture, soft tissue over right foot and leg treated as inpatient from 04.04.2023 to 07.04.2023 and he underwent surgery using implants.
He is still under follow up treatment.

That he has spent Rs. 9,00,000/- towards hospital, conveyance,
medicine, food and nourishment charges and other incidental charges.

He is completely bed redden,
getting head ache and giddiness often, cannot walk, stand, sit squat on the floor, cannot use Indian toilet, cannot lift or carry weight, cannot ride or drive vehicle and undergoing deep mental shock,
pain and suffering, since the injuries caused permanent in nature due to permanent disability as he is not able to do any work.
4. That prior to accident he was hale and healthy, working as an Fruit vendor and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
After the accident, he is not able to do any work and lost his entire earnings.
The accident is solely due to rash and negligent riding of rider of Opponent vehicle.

That Bellanduru Traffic police have registered the Crime No.47/2023 against the driver of Car vehicle bearing reg.No.KL-22-H-9642 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC and on investigation,
they have filed the charge sheet against him.
Respondent No.1 is R.C owner and Respondent No.2 is insurance company of the offending vehicle and the insurance was valid at the time of accident.
Therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with cost &
interest in the above case.
5. In response to notice, respondent no.1 has not appeared before this court and remained absent.
Hence, he is placed exparte.

2 6.

2nd respondent insurance company appeared through his counsel and filed objections/written statement admitting the validity of insurance policy of Car bearing No.KL-22-H-9642 and contended that it is subjected to terms and conditions of the said policy.
It disputed that compliance of Sec.134 (c) and 156(8) of Motor Vehicle Act.
Manner of accident alleged by the petitioner is disputed.
That the driver of the Car was not having valid and effective Driving license as on the date of accident and thereby vehicle owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The age, occupation, income and permanent disability alleged by the petitioner all are denied.

As per the crime documents, the petitioners was walking on the road and he was not suppose to walk on the road, hence there is gross violation of the traffic rules as such petitioner himself was solely negligent.
Therefore, this petition is not maintainable for one's own negligence.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings,following issues are framed:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 04.01.2023 at about 3.30 pm he was pedestrian walking on extreme left side of Sarjapura Main Road, near Lakasa Restaurant, Jayamareddy Layout, Kasavanahalli, Bengaluru, at that time driver of one Car bearing Reg. No. KL-22-H-9642 came from behind in reverse gear in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
2. Whether the 2nd respondent proves driver of Car bearing No.KL-22-H-9642 was not holding valid DL at the time of accident?
3. Whether respondent No.2 proves petitioner was negligent in walking on the road?
4. Whetter the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability, if any?
5. Whether the is the petitioner is entitled or compensation? If so by whom and what is the quantum?
6. What Order or Award?
8.
To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.22 documents are marked on his behalf.
Yadunandan H.L., Deputy Manager, Manipal hospital is examined as P.W.2.
Through him Ex.P.23 to 28 documents are marked.
Doctor by name S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria hospital, is examined as P.W.3 and through him Ex.P.29 and 30 documents are marked.
On the contrary, no evidence is led by respondent side and both side evidence is closed.
9. Heard learned counsel for both sides.
Perused the records.

10. On taking into consideration the entire evidence and arguments placed before this Tribunal, my answers to, Issue no.1 - Partly in the affirmative, Issue no.2 - In the negative, Issue no.3 - Partly in the affirmative,, Issue no.4 - Partly in the affirmative, Issue no.5 - Partly in the affirmative Issue no.6 - As per final orders for the following;
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1 and ISSUE NO.3 : Since these two issues are on the point of negligence and contributory negligence, they are taken together for discussion.
It is the case of petitioner that, he sustained injuries in the road traffic accident which occurred on 04.01.2023.
It appears date is wrongly mentioned in the claim petition as in FIR it is mentioned as 04.04.2023.
It is contended that due to alleged rash and negligent driving of driver of Car bearing no. KL-22-H-9642 petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It is stated in the petition that he was pedestrian walking on extreme left side of road, the driver of car came behind in reverse gear in rash and negligent manner and dashed to petitioner.
To prove this fact he entered into witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
In chief examination he reiterated petition averments.

He has produced FIR,
first information, certified copy of plea in CC No.3742/2023, spot mahazar, IMV report, Final report, MLC extract, wound certificate at Ex.P1 to 12 and discharge summary at Ex.P.20.
12.

As per first information, one Sri. Mastan Reddy who is son of petitioner gave first information to police stating that his father was walking on the main road on 04.04.2023 at about 3.30 p.m., at that time the driver of Car bearing No. KL-22-H- 9642 came in rash and negligent manner in reverse gear and dashed to his father and his father sustained grievous injuries to his knees and shifted to Manipal Hospital in the same car.
There doctors examined him and found that the fractures in the knees treated him, therefore action may be taken against driver of the car.
On the basis of this first information Bellanduru Police have registered in crime No.47/2023 against the car driver for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.
On the next day of the accident spot mahzar was conducted in which the first informant shown the accident spot, as per mahazar it is main road of Kasavanahalli, Jayaramareddy Layout, 2nd Cross road.
As per sketch accident has taken place almost middle of the road and sketch shows petitioner was not exactly on his extreme left side of the road.
Charge sheet is filed against the diver of the car.
As per wound certificate issued by Manipal hospital due to RTA petitioner was admitted and he had sustained fracture of medial malleolus of right ankle and multiple abrasion right leg and foot.
These documents goes to show that petitioner sustained RTA and he was admitted in the hospital.
The first information was given to police attributing negligence on the car driver, no counter complaint is given by the car driver about the negligence of petitioner.
The car driver has pleaded guilty of the offence and paid fine.
He has not questioned the FIR or final report.
Therefore all these documents show that driver of the car was negligent in the accident.
13. But 2nd respondent contended that petitioner was negligent in walking on the road.
To prove this fact the respondent not led evidence, but he cross examined PW1 and relied upon the spot sketch produced by the petitioner himself at Ex.P6.
In the cross examination of PW1, it is suggested that since the petitioner was walking in the middle of the road accident has taken place.

The said Nimmanapalli Krishnareddy vs Tony Sebastian on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140476559/
4 suggestion is denied by PW1.

sentences.text: But as per Ex.P6 spot sketch prepared by the police, the spot of accident is almost in the middle of the road and not at the edge or side of the road.
Meaning, the petitioner was walking almost in the middle of the road which is against the traffic rules.

Therefore,
there is some negligence on part of petitioner also.
If he were walk on extreme left side of the road or on the foot path the accident could have been avoided.
However, the car driver, was more negligent as, while taking reverse of the car, he should have observed the traffic or movement of people on the road.
Therefore in the opinion of this court there is negligence of both side in the accident.
In that view of the matter, in the opinion of this court, negligence on part of the petitioner is 20% and negligence on part of the car driver is 80%.
Therefore, these two issues are answered Partly in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:
2nd respondent contended that the driver of car was not having D.L to drive the vehicle, but to prove this fact no evidence is led.
Therefore, this issue is not proved.
Accordingly, I hold this Issue in the Negative.
15. ISSUE NO.4 :
Respondents disputed the age of the petitioner.
He has not produced any document to prove his age.
In the cross examination it is suggested that petitioner aged about 68 years at the time of accident.
He denied the same.
In the MLC extract his age is mentioned as 68 years.
but in FIR it is mentioned as 62 years.
His Aadhaar Card copy is available in record.
It shows the petitioner was born on 1962.
The said document is not marked in the evidence.
But, even if his year of birth is considered as 1962, he was aged 61 years at the time of accident.
Hence in my view, it is proper to hold that petitioner was aged 61 years at the time of accident.
16. Respondents disputed the occupation of the petitioner while the petitioner contended that he used to work as fruit vendor.
But, no evidence is placed to prove or disprove his occupation.
Hence notional income of Rs.16,000/- is considered keeping in mind the cost of living and accident having taken place in the year 2023.
17. Petitioner contended that he is suffering from permanent disability due to the injury sustained by his which is disputed by respondents.

As per the case of petitioner he sustained fracture of right ankle medial malleolus fracture soft tissue injury over right foot and leg, underwent surgery in the form of ORIF with CC screws for medial malleolus, SSG by plastic surgery team under Anesthesia on 05.04.2023.
To prove the disability, a non treated doctor got examined as PW3 and according to clinical examination made by PW3, total disability of right lower limb is 31% and to the whole body is 16%.
It is settled law that, doctor can only assess physical disability and cannot assess the functional disability having regard to avocation of the patient.
As contended by the petitioner he was working as fruit vendor.
Since petitioner is said to be fruit vendor and cannot sit without pain, injury in lower limb will come in the way of his occupation and may affect his income.

As per the evidence of doctor the fracture is united, petitioner has complained about pain and there is wasting of right lower limb, this tribunal is of the opinion that disability affecting the income of the of the petitioner is at 10%.
Accordingly I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.5 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of vehicle bearing No. KL-22-H-9642.

There is nexus between the injuries Nimmanapalli Krishnareddy vs Tony Sebastian on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140476559/
5 sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings:

While the pain and suffering can only be experienced and no proof could be produced to show as to how much pain one has suffered due to injury, law requires court should assess the pain and award compensation.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he underwent operation.
he was in hospital for 4 days with advice to take complete rest, continue medicine and to take follow up treatment, which is undoubtedly painful and caused agony.

Hence for pain and sufferings, petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.30,000/-
(ii) For Medical expenses:
As per medical bills at Ex. P.18, petitioner has paid Rs.6,71,982/- to various hospitals in which he took treatment.
The said payment of bill is disputed by the respondent No.2.
he got summoned the billing superintendent of Manipal hospital to clarify about the bills.
But even after bailable warrant was issued, the witness could not be secured.
Hence case is proceeded.
The contention of the 2nd respondent is that, petitioner while counting the bills, double counted some advance bills and shown almost 6 lakhs as the payment which is not correct.
According to 2 nd respondent only amount paid as per bills as found in the I.P. records.

On perusal of inpatient records which are summoned and produced at Ex.P.26 to 28 the amount which is paid by the petitioner is Rs.2,65,302/- which is inpatient final bill and medicine bills of Rs.14,132/-.

Therefore,
petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs. 2,79,434/-.
(iii) For Food and nourishment:
Whether there is special diet advice from the doctor or not, to recover from the grievous physical pain and injury, need of nutritious food and nourishment cannot be ignored.
The petitioner was in hospital for 04 days.
Accident took place in the year 2023.
Considering the cost of living, food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded, Rs.500/- x 04 days = Rs.2,000/-it will meet the ends of justice.
(iv) For Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 4 days someone should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of his in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence attendant charges has to be awarded.
if per day Rs.500/- is awarded, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 04 days =Rs.2,000/-is awarded.
(v) For Loss of income during laid up period: Petitioner was inpatient for 4 days and he underwent operation.
Minimum 3 months is required to recover from such operation in view of grievous injury.
Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 3 months including in patient period and hence compensation for loss of income during laid up period is Rs.16,000/- x 3 = 48,000/-
( vi )
Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted to hospital from the spot of accident.
he took treatment at various hospitals as mentioned in the petition.
The same is proved to medical records.
He still needs to go for removal of implants.

He has spent money for conveyance for the Nimmanapalli Krishnareddy vs Tony Sebastian on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140476559/
6 purpose of treatment.
He is further required to go for follow up treatment for removal of implants etc.
He has produced cab bills at Ex.P.19, but they are not proved by the person who issued them.
Therefore, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.

(vii) For Loss of future income due to Disability : As per the findings given to issue no.2 functional disability of the petitioner is assessed at the rate of 10% Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is per month income 16,000/- x 12 months x 10% disability x 7 multiplier to the age group above 61-65 years.
Hence towards loss of future income due to disability petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,34,400/-
(viii) For Physical discomfort & loss of amenities of life:
As per the evidence of doctor, petitioner cannot lift any weight in his right upper limb and suffers pain and discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of his normal enjoyment of life.

Hence, petitioner is entitled to compensation for physical discomfort and loss of amenities of to the tune of Rs.40,000/-
(ix)
For Future medical expenses:
P.W.3 has deposed that implants has not been removed and for that Rs.30,000/- is required.
Removal of implants is necessary for the well being of the petitioner.
Therefore, for future medical expenses compensation of Rs.25,000/- has to be awarded.
(x) For loss of future prospects:
Even in injury cases, court has to consider whether future prospect is affected by the accidental injuries to victim.
In this case, on considering the oral and documentary evidence no such loss of future prospect is evident in respect of petitioner.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

19. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,52,668/- in respect of injuries sustained by his in the Road traffic accident precisely under the following heads;
Sl Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i. Pain & Sufferings 30,000/-
ii. Medical expenses 2,79,434/-
iii. Food and nourishment 2,000/-
iv. Attendant charges 2,000/-
v. Loss of income during laid up 48,000/-
 period vi.

Conveyance charges 5,000/-
vii. Loss of income due to disability 1,34,400/-
viii Physical discomfort and loss of 40,000/-
 amenities of life ix.

Future medical expenses 25,000/-

7 x. Loss of future prospects Nil

Minus contributory negligence on - Rs.1,13,166/-
 part of the petitioner to the extent  of 20%
 Grand
Liability:

Since respondent no.2 has admitted the validity of the insurance policy of Car bearing No.KL-22-H-9642 as on the date of accident it is liable to indemnify the insured and pay the compensation to petitioner.

In view of settled law on the point of interest, he is entitled to 6%
interest on the award amount except on future medical expenses.

Hence, I answer this issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
21. ISSUE NO.6:-
In view of above reasons, I pass following :
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,52,668/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.4,27,668-from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).
The respondent no.2 is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
After such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation in his favour without making FD.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the Award accordingly.

Total Rs.5,65,834/-
Minus contributory negligence on - Rs.1,13,166/-
 part of the petitioner to the extent  of 20%
 Grand
In view of settled law on the point of interest, he is entitled to 6%
interest on the award amount except on future medical expenses.
In view of above reasons, I pass following :
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,52,668/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.4,27,668-from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).
The respondent no.2 is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
After such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation in his favour without making FD.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the Award accordingly.
